title: Where do the corners go when a square is flipped?
description: A square with its corners labelled is flipped over its vertical middle line, and the new place of each corner is found. Keeko doubts that the corners move, because the square looks the same.
teaching_notes: One idea: a reflection sends each corner to the matching place at the same height on the other side of the line. Watch for students who say nothing moves because the flipped square looks unchanged.

source: A square has corners labelled A (top left), B (top right), C (bottom right), D (bottom left). When the square is reflected along the vertical line of symmetry, where do A, B, C and D go?
video_script.why: The child follows each labelled corner of a square across a vertical line and sees that the corners swap places.
video_script.substitution: Draw the vertical line through the middle and move each corner to the same height on the other side.
video_script.anchor: A square with corners A at the top left, B at the top right, C at the bottom right and D at the bottom left, and a vertical dotted line through its middle
video_script.wrong_answer: every corner stays in its own place
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says every corner stays in its own place because the flipped square looks the same. Following the labels shows A landing where B was, so the idea is struck out.
video_script.payoff_line: Each corner lands at the same height on the other side.

final_answer.value: A takes the place of B, B the place of A, D the place of C, and C the place of D
final_answer.spoken: corner eigh takes the place of B, B takes the place of eigh, D takes the place of C, and C takes the place of D

hold_back: A takes the place of B
never_show: the new places of the corners before their steps
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
Flipping a shape over a line of symmetry is a reflection.
A corner moves across the line to the place at the same height and the same distance on the other side.
A and B are at the same height on opposite sides of the vertical line, so they swap places.
D and C are at the same height on opposite sides of the vertical line, so they swap places.
The square looks the same afterwards, but the labels have moved.
video_script.design: One idea: a reflection moves each point to the matching place across the line. Assumes the child knows the square and its vertical fold. The labelled square stays on the board from the hook to the end.
